entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Interscope Geffen A&M (IGA) is one of the most powerful label groups in the global music industry — formed from the combination of Interscope Records (founded 1989 by Jimmy Iovine and Ted Field), Geffen Records (founded 1980 by David Geffen), and A&M Records (founded 1962 by Herb Alpert and Jerry Moss) into a single major label group under Universal Music Group, collectively representing an extraordinary catalog including artists across virtually every genre of popular music from the 1960s to the present.

A&M Records was one of the great independent labels before corporate acquisition: Herb Alpert and Jerry Moss built A&M from the Alpert-created Tijuana Brass sound to one of the most artist-friendly major labels, signing artists like Carole King, Janet Jackson, Joe Cocker, Supertramp, and The Police (all of whose foundational catalogs are now in the IGA portfolio). Geffen Records similarly represented David Geffen's artist-focused vision with artists including John Lennon, Joni Mitchell, Nirvana, Guns N' Roses, and Aerosmith.

Interscope itself, under Jimmy Iovine, became one of the defining labels of 1990s-2000s American music — signing Tupac Shakur, Dr. Dre, Eminem, Nine Inch Nails, No Doubt, and Lady Gaga. The combination of these three label legacies under Universal Music Group creates one of the world's most valuable music catalogs, though critics note that the consolidation of the music industry into three major groups (Universal, Sony, Warner) raises significant concerns about music industry concentration and independent artist representation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Interscope Geffen A&M — combining the catalogs of Interscope, Geffen, and A&M into one of the world's most valuable music archives — is historically significant as a monument to music industry consolidation and the commercial organization of six decades of recorded American popular music.
